text:
alex: Heads-up: we're seeing a pronounced tail-latency spike (~3x) from gpu-pool-a starting ~10:23 UTC. Traces point to long waits in admission_control and a fallback to a slower kernel variant. Anyone oncall?

maria: Yep, noticed at 10:22. Throughput drops ~20% during the spike and microbatch sizes jump between 1 and 4 repeatedly.

yun: Pushed a quick sampling from profiler. Paste: 
```
kernel_selected: aten_fused_v2
latency_ms: 1187
queued_ms: 460
kernel_dispatch_ms: 700
model: gptx-30b-quant
microbatch_sizes: [1,4,1,2,1,4]
kvcache_evictions: high (shard=7)
```

sam: That pattern screams admission admission throttling + kernel selector oscillation. If microbatch keeps bouncing the selector may flip to a compatibility path that's slower.

leo: I can confirm kvcache shard-7 shows a burst of evictions aligned with these spikes. Noisy neighbor? Multiple small requests causing frequent KV evict+reload.

alex: Can someone run `curl -s http://metrics.local/pool/gpu-pool-a?window=5m | jq .` and dump scheduler/admission stats? Want queued lengths + admission rejections.

maria: Dump attached (snippet): 
```
{"time":"10:22:30","queued":128,"admit_rate":0.62,"rejections":36,"microbatch_mean":1.8}
{"time":"10:23:00","queued":402,"admit_rate":0.28,"rejections":210,"microbatch_mean":2.6}
```

qa-jen: I reproduced locally with a clustered arrival pattern - short bursts of single-token requests mixed with some long sequences. Admission controller oscillates, scheduler forms tiny microbatches then back to singletons. Tail latency jumps.

sam: Quick mitigation options: 1) pin kernel selector to baseline kernel for the affected model/version 2) add hysteresis to admission control (simple backoff) 3) bump kvcache shard limit or isolate noisy tenant. Which do we want first?

alex: Start with (1) and (2) in that order. Pinning is lowest-risk and fast. Also roll a canary with kvcache eviction logging enabled.

yun: Pin command to config service: 
```
POST /config/pools/gpu-pool-a/overrides
{"model":"gptx-30b-quant","kernel_force":"baseline_aten_v1"}
```

leo: I'll open a kvcache telemetry filter for shard-7 and increase retention for 10m.

infra-bot: deploy-bot triggered: canary deploy starting for gpu-pool-a with config override (canary-id=canary-1850012345).

sam: Also I'm prototyping an admission backoff patch: add a 250ms soft-hold when accept_rate < 0.4 to avoid rapid oscillations. Will push to canary branch.

maria: After pinning kernels we saw immediate improvement: queued down to ~90, tail p95 fell from 1.2s to 430ms within two minutes. kvcache evictions still a bit elevated but lower.

alex: Good. Can we get a flamegraph of the slow path to validate kernel-selection cost differential? Yun?

yun: Uploaded flamegraph here: https://internal/graphs/1850012345/flame (contains kernel switch and path cost). Short summary: fused_v2 spends ~65% of time in kernel runtime overhead when microbatch < 2; baseline_aten_v1 is more stable at low batch sizes.

qa-jen: Regression hypothesis: commit b12c3e4 changed kernel selection thresholds to prefer fused kernels for small seqs; that reduced perf in adversarial arrival patterns. I can run bisect if we want concrete commit.

sam: I'll revert selection tweak in canary and add a unit test simulating bursty arrival to catch this. Also will add a metric: kernel_switches_per_minute.

alex: Please create a postmortem doc item with timeline and next-steps: pinning -> revert -> admission backoff -> kvcache shard inspection. Assign owners.

maria: Filing: https://internal/incidents/rt-1850012345 (adding logs and perf graphs).

infra-bot: canary-deploy successful: canary-1850012345 -> 10% traffic. Monitoring for 15m.

leo: Early signals look good. p95 trending down on canary nodes. Noisy tenant isolation scheduled for tomorrow if eviction persists.

alex: Thanks everyone. Action items: sam (revert + backoff PR), yun (flamegraph + perf numbers), leo (kvcache telemetry), qa-jen (add regression test), maria (postmortem writeup). Ping me when PRs are up. :thumbsup:
